PubMed record 37466480 (Cannabis Cannabinoid Res, 2024) records that tetrahydrocannabinol-O-acetate is colloquially known as THCO. This is the nomenclature basis for registering `THCO` as the spelling variant of the query text `THC-O`; it supports the name, never a single chemical identity (ISS-20261104-TAX-029). External reference: recorded by URL and observation time, never hashed (external_unverifiable).

PubChem CID 198013 is the delta9-Tetrahydrocannabinol acetate record: synonym THC-O-ACETATE, CAS 23132-17-4, molecular formula C23H32O3. It records what `THC-O` / `THC-O-acetate` names, not that the `THCO` query string has one identity: the same abbreviation also denotes tetrahydrocannabiorcol (C17H22O2; see ev-cayman-33762-delta8-thco and ev-cayman-33763-delta9-thco). No exactMatch is derived from this record for compound_thc_o (ISS-20261104-TAX-029). External reference: recorded by URL and observation time, never hashed (external_unverifiable).

PubMed record 37381980 (J Psychoactive Drugs, 2024) uses the written form THC-O-Acetate in academic usage. Supports the spelling of the canonical query text, not the chemical identity of the THCO string (ISS-20261104-TAX-029). External reference: recorded by URL and observation time, never hashed (external_unverifiable).

PubMed record 36508081 (J Med Toxicol, 2023) uses the written form THC-O Acetate in academic usage. Supports the spelling of the canonical query text, not the chemical identity of the THCO string (ISS-20261104-TAX-029). External reference: recorded by URL and observation time, never hashed (external_unverifiable).

Delta-9-THCO reference standard: delta9-THCO, CAS 22972-65-2, molecular formula C17H22O2. This is tetrahydrocannabiorcol, not the acetate: it shows that the abbreviation THCO also names a different substance, so a `THCO` query variant cannot be read as one chemical identity (ISS-20261104-TAX-029). External reference: recorded by URL and observation time, never hashed (external_unverifiable).

Delta-8-THCO reference standard: delta8-THCO, CAS 22972-64-1, molecular formula C17H22O2. Together with the delta9 isomer it shows two distinct THCO reference substances that are not the acetate, so a `THCO` query variant cannot be read as one chemical identity (ISS-20261104-TAX-029). External reference: recorded by URL and observation time, never hashed (external_unverifiable).

FDA GSRS approved record for CANNABIELSOIN (substanceClass chemical, definitionLevel COMPLETE, version 7): names CANNABIELSOIN / CANNABIELSOIN A / CANNABIELSOIN I / CBE; codes CAS 52025-76-0, PubChem 162113, FDA UNII 2ERD6V6652; formula C21H30O3. This is the identity and identifier basis for the 2026-11-11 CBE update (ISS-20261111-TAX-040 addendum). It does not establish natural occurrence, route/origin or query-result content. External reference: recorded by URL and observation time, never hashed (external_unverifiable).

Wikidata Q22668702: en label 'cannabielsoin', ja label 'カンナビエルソイン', alias 'cannabielsoin A'; CAS 52025-76-0, UNII 2ERD6V6652, PubChem 162113, formula C21H30O3. Used for the preferred labels and exactMatch in compound_cbe; not an independent natural-occurrence source. External reference: no hash (external_unverifiable).

Yamamoto et al. 1988 (J Pharmacobiodyn 11:833-838): cannabielsoin (CBE) identified as a novel metabolite formed from cannabidiol by guinea-pig hepatic microsomal enzymes; little activity in mouse pentobarbital-sleep and body-temperature tests. Supports the CBE = cannabielsoin name and metabolic formation from CBD; it does not establish intact-plant natural occurrence or the content of query results.

Yamamoto et al. 1989 (J Pharmacobiodyn 12:488-494): mechanism of biological formation of cannabielsoin from cannabidiol in guinea pig, mouse, rat and rabbit; hepatic microsomes, NADPH and molecular oxygen required, cytochrome P-450 inhibitors suppress, species differences recorded. Supports metabolic formation from CBD; not natural-plant occurrence or query content.

Yamamoto et al. 1991 (Pharmacol Biochem Behav 40:541-546): cannabielsoin identified as a new metabolite of cannabidiol in mammals; CBE-type metabolites formed via 1S,2R-epoxides. Supports the mammalian-metabolite description; not natural-plant occurrence or query content.

Hartsel et al. 1983 (Planta Med 48:17-19): suspension cultures of Cannabis sativa and Saccharum officinarum biotransform cannabidiol to cannabielsoin, producing both C-1 stereoisomers. Supports formation by Cannabis cell cultures; it is not a direct isolation from intact plants and does not establish query-result content.

Haghdoost et al. 2024 (Biomedicines 12:1551; DOI 10.3390/biomedicines12071551; PMCID PMC11275175): the paper describes CBE as a non-enzymatic phytocannabinoid whose natural presence in Cannabis sativa has been established, and also as a CBD oxidation byproduct and minor mammalian metabolite; in-vitro S-CBE acted as a CB1 cAMP agonist (EC50 3.7 uM) with no beta-arrestin agonist activity up to 12 uM. Supports the compound_minor phytocannabinoid placement and provides pharmacological context; it does not support Japanese market presence or the content of Google Trends / YouTube results.

PubChem CID 59444380: title 'Cannabicyclol', stereospecified IUPAC name (1R,9R,12S,14R)-9,13,13-trimethyl-5-pentyl-8-oxatetracyclo[7.4.1.02,7.012,14]tetradeca-2,4,6-trien-3-ol, formula C21H30O2, CAS-like synonym 21366-63-2, UNII MP5WZK8M5U. External reference: no hash (external_unverifiable).

Haghdoost et al. 2025 (J Nat Prod 88; DOI 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.4c00977): the abstract calls cannabicyclol ((+/-)-CBL) 'a minor phytocannabinoid' and reports acid-catalysed conversion of cannabichromene (CBC) to CBL (montmorillonite K30, 60% yield), with the structure confirmed by X-ray crystallography; in vitro CBL acted as a 5-HT1A positive allosteric modulator. Supports the name, the compound_minor placement and an acid-catalysed (non-enzymatic) conversion from CBC; it does not establish enzymatic biosynthesis in the living plant, plant quantities, regulatory status or the content of query results.

Forensic Sci Int 2021 (DOI 10.1016/j.forsciint.2021.110773): 16 phytocannabinoids, including cannabicyclol and cannabigerolic acid, were quantified in seized cannabis, medical cannabis, Sativex and dronabinol samples. Supports that CBL and CBGA are phytocannabinoids detected in cannabis material; post-harvest conversion and product processing are not excluded, so it does not establish the biosynthetic route or query-result content.

Wikidata Q27135612: en label 'cannabigerolic acid', alias '(E)-3-(3,7-Dimethyl-2,6-octadienyl)-2,4-dihydroxy-6-pentylbenzoic acid'; CAS 25555-57-1, PubChem CID 6449999, ChEBI 67081, formula C22H32O4. Used for the CBGA preferred label and exactMatch in compound_cbga. External reference: no hash (external_unverifiable).

Used for the CBGA identity and identifiers; the record states no natural-occurrence quantity, route or regulatory claim. External reference: no hash (external_unverifiable).

ChEBI 67081 'cannabigerolic acid': a dihydroxybenzoic acid that is olivetolic acid with a geranyl group at position 3, described as 'a biosynthetic precursor to delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol'; synonym (E)-3-(3,7-dimethyl-2,6-octadienyl)-2,4-dihydroxy-6-pentylbenzoic acid (not obsolete). Supports the identity, the precursor description and the exactMatch; the decarboxylation to CBG is supported by the literature entries, not by this definition. External reference: no hash (external_unverifiable).

PubChem CID 6449999: title 'Cannabigerolic Acid', IUPAC name 3-[(2E)-3,7-dimethylocta-2,6-dienyl]-2,4-dihydroxy-6-pentylbenzoic acid, formula C22H32O4, CAS-like synonym 25555-57-1, ChEBI:67081, UNII 80I4ZM847Y. Corroborates the GSRS, Wikidata and ChEBI records for CBGA. External reference: no hash (external_unverifiable).

J Nat Prod 2019 (DOI 10.1021/acs.jnatprod.9b00600): describes Cannabis sativa phytocannabinoids as occurring in neutral forms or as acid precursors that dominate in the plant, and lists cannabigerolic acid (CBGA) among the phytocannabinoid acids administered to mice. Supports the compound_minor placement of CBGA as a phytocannabinoid other than the major pair; it does not support Japanese market presence or query-result content.

Int J Mol Sci 2022 (DOI 10.3390/ijms23147929): states that CBG is generated during the non-enzymatic decarboxylation of cannabigerolic acid, described as a key compound in phytocannabinoid biosynthesis and the precursor of various phytocannabinoids. Supports the CBGA/CBG distinction recorded in the compound_cbga scopeNote; no skos:related link to compound_cbg is asserted. External reference: no hash (external_unverifiable).

MHLW grant report (令和5年度厚生労働行政推進調査事業費補助金, 分担研究報告書 'Marijuana/THC/CBD edible に関わる問題点', 研究分担者 山本経之): a Japanese-language scientific report that lists natural cannabinoids and writes カンナビシクロール（CBL）and カンナビエルソイン（CBE）, and describes カンナビゲロール酸 as the start of the CBD/THC pathway. Used only for the Japanese labels of CBL and CBGA; it is not a regulatory-status source for Japan and does not support query-result content. External reference: no hash (external_unverifiable).

J-GLOBAL (JST) chemical substance record: カンナビゲロール酸 / Cannabigerolic acid, formula C22H32O4, InChIKey SEEZIOZEUUMJME-FOWTUZBSSA-N, other names including CBGA. Used for the Japanese label カンナビゲロール酸 of compound_cbga. External reference: no hash (external_unverifiable).

MHLW notice '指定薬物を指定する省令が公布されました' (令和6年厚生労働省令第81号): promulgated 2024-05-01, in force 2024-05-11. Structural group 1 (6a,7,8,10a-tetrahydro-6,6,9-trimethyl-6H-dibenzo[b,d]pyran with one hydroxyl or acetoxy at position 1 and a straight-chain C3-C8 alkyl at position 3, no other substituents; narcotics excluded, 麻薬を除く) and group 2 (the 6a,7,10,10a-tetrahydro series, same exclusion) include the acetoxy forms; the appendix (https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/11126000/001250830.pdf) lists Δ9-THCP-O-acetate and Δ8-THCP-O-acetate at n=7. Used only for the statutory structural-group coverage of the two THCP-O-acetate isomers; it does not establish the content or legality of any product, route/origin, natural occurrence, pharmacology or safety. External reference: no hash (external_unverifiable).

Tanaka, Ito & Kikura-Hanajiri 2025 (Drug Test Anal 17(9):1795-1802, DOI 10.1002/dta.3883): analysed seven oil products and one herbal product distributed online by GC-MS, LC-PDA-MS and NMR, and identified Δ9-THCP-O (acetate) and Δ9-THCP-O-butanoate. Supports the Δ9 acetate as an analysed substance and distinguishes THCP-O-butanoate as a different ester; the Δ8 acetate it identifies is Δ8-THC-O (the C5 analogue), not Δ8-THCP-O-acetate, so it does not identify the THCP-O-acetate family as a whole or the content of any query result. External reference: recorded by URL and observation time, never hashed (external_unverifiable).

Wikidata Q122689235, en label 'THCP-O-acetate', no ja label: InChIKey OXMUZNKOOOITQD-NHCUHLMSSA-N and PubChem CID 172677450, i.e. the Δ9 record; no CAS statement. Moreno-Sanz 2016 (Cannabis Cannabinoid Res 1:124-130) describes Δ9-THCA-A (2-carboxy-THC) as the acidic precursor of Δ9-THC in Cannabis and notes that the literature has used 'THCA' loosely for several acidic derivatives; it also records THCA-B (4-carboxy-THC) as a distinct isomer first reported by Mechoulam et al. 1969. Supports the nomenclature and structural distinction behind the Δ9-THCA-A and THCA-B search topics. It does not establish the content of any query result or product, natural occurrence in Japan, or a single external registry record for the registered strings (ISS-20261111-TAX-041).
